text:
maria_support: Escalation from acct-4321: SSE chat stream sometimes ends with a truncated final event — last JSON object is cut, and finish_reason is missing. Customer sees partial response and then a silent connection close on reconnect. Repro steps + output below, cc @jon_sre @sam_eng :eyes:

jon_sre: Thanks — can you paste the minimal repro and any runtime logs you have?

maria_support: Repro (curl):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REQ-TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize long doc"}],"stream":true}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat
```
Observed stream tail (client received):
```
event: message
data: {"id":"tok_abc123","choices":[{"delta":"In summary, the system","index":0}}

// connection drops here; note the final JSON is malformed (extra `}` removed)
```
No `event: done` or `finish_reason` field delivered. When the client reconnects with Resume-From, they sometimes get duplicated partial tokens and then nothing.

sam_eng: Could be a flush/connection-teardown issue. Any proxy in front? token TTL? client side reconnect behavior?

maria_support: Customer is behind our hosted endpoint (Fastly fronting), TTL for the long-running token is 5m. This repro was within 2m. They reported both browser and server-side clients (node fetch + curl).

jon_sre: Pasting runtime egress log snippet from the time window: 
```
[1769632123] conn=3421 stream_id=78 write_bytes=7634 status=200 event=stream_chunk
[1769632228] conn=3421 stream_id=78 err="write_timeout" code=499 flush_ok=false
[1769632228] conn=3421 stream_id=78 connection_closed_by_peer=true
[1769632229] conn=3421 stream_id=78 final_chunk_attempted=true flush_return=EPIPE
```
That looks like the backend attempted to write the final SSE chunk but got EPIPE on flush. finish_reason was set server-side, but the final event didn't hit the wire.

sam_eng: EPIPE on final flush + Fastly in front = likely intermediate TCP reset before kernel send completes. Two hypotheses: Fastly idle timeout or an L7 rule closing the socket before FIN. Also Resume-From behavior can double-consume if we don't persist a terminal marker.

maria_support: Customer's Fastly config uses a 90s streaming idle timeout. Some sessions here are ~95-100s. Could be a match. They said sometimes it works, sometimes not.

sam_eng: Short-term mitigation: 1) add a periodic SSE heartbeat event every 15s to keep the proxy alive; 2) on server side, ensure we write a tiny final padding chunk before closing so kernel can push it (e.g., write "\\n" after final event and call flush with backoff). Longer-term: add an explicit final SSE event header we persist to resume store so Resume-From can detect terminal marker even if final chunk lost.

jon_sre: Agreed. Can we add a small change to runtime to retry final flush up to N times on EPIPE? Also add instrumentation to surface "final_chunk_written" boolean to Console. That helps correlate with customer reports.

sam_eng: I can do a small runtime patch: retry flush x3 with 100ms backoff and mark final_chunk_written only after syscall returns success. Will open PR and do a canary.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued: runtime/fix-final-flush-retries -> env=canary-2 -> sha=ab12cd3 (owner: sam_eng)

maria_support: Thanks. Please reference support ticket #4321 in the PR and set Console alert for missing finish_reason > 5 occurrences/hour. Customer is blocked on reliable streaming for large responses.

jon_sre: Also adding a Grafana panel for EPIPE/final-flush-failures. If we see correlation with 90s connections, we'll notify ops to talk to CDN team about adjusting keep-alive.

maria_support: I'll update the customer with the mitigation (heartbeat + watch for canary) and ask them to test with a heartbeat header.

sam_eng: Note: sample heartbeat SSE frame to add if needed: `event: heartbeat\ndata: {"ts":<unix>}\n\n` — will include behind feature flag.

maria_support: Closing loop here for the ticket until canary results are in. Thanks :thumbsup:
